reviews.text: Would give it no stars if I could. The vet didn’t seem to care what I was saying. Was reluctant to take bloods or give fluids through IV even though he hadn’t eaten or drank in days. Showed a picture of the tapeworm she threw up and prescribed her spot on treatment for hookworm so had to attend pet hospital for an emergency app after another 24hrs of no food or water or passing urine. I have been bringing my cat here due to loss of weight for months and they have done nothing. Almost cost my cat her life.

I would not recommend this veterinary practice based on my experience.

My dog’s mouth was bleeding heavily, so I booked an appointment on Monday. We saw Robyn Smith, who said it was likely a dental problem, prescribed antibiotics, and told us to come back the following Monday. I don’t feel a thorough examination of his mouth was carried out, and blood tests or scans were not offered.

When my dog didn’t improve, I went back on Wednesday for a second opinion with a different vet. Sadly, I was told his mouth was covered in cancerous tumours and the kindest option was to put him to sleep that day. I was also told that if we’d waited until Monday, his airway could have closed.

This has been heartbreaking. I believe that if a full examination had been carried out at the first appointment, his condition may have been identified sooner and he could have been spared unnecessary pain. While I appreciate the care from the second vet, I was extremely disappointed with the initial treatment and would not recommend this practice.

I honestly can’t thank the team at PDSA Vet Hospital in Leeds enough. The vet nurses and staff are absolutely incredible and deserve so much more recognition for everything they do.

I was really anxious about taking my dog because she is reactive. From our very first visit, every single member of staff has gone above and beyond to make both of us feel comfortable. They never made me feel judged and they always handled my dog with so much patience, kindness and understanding. They genuinely put me at ease every time we visited.

My dog recently had to undergo spaying surgery, and I was so nervous beforehand, especially after reading some negative reviews online. I was honestly in two minds about going ahead with the operation because of what I’d read. Looking back now, I’m so glad I trusted them. The care she received was outstanding, and I was genuinely blown away by how quickly she recovered.

I’ve now visited the hospital around six times, and every single appointment has reinforced just how dedicated this team is. They always take the time to listen, explain everything clearly, and do everything they can to help.

I know every pet and every situation is different, but based on my own experience, I honestly couldn’t fault this team one bit. They work incredibly hard under what I can only imagine are very challenging circumstances, yet they continue to provide exceptional care.

Unfortunately I had to put my cat down there yesterday (yes I'm still crying) . She was elderly. The staff there are so considerate and empathetic and wonderful. I was allowed sometime with her before they took her away. The only thing I've got a problem with is the way people talk to the staff there. I think they should have security. No one and I mean no one deserves to be spoke to like that because they haven't been brought up correctly ( the mother was just as bad!). The staff handled a situation extremely well and with dignity considering the lowlife that was shouting at them at the time was obviously unhinged in some way. The guy on the desk kept his cool considering he was being shouted at for absolutely no reason, it was just word vomit exiting the toothless mouth Infront of him, So I just want to say I hope you are okay! And I apologise on behalf of that lemon. So even though my experience was sad, I think the staff are exceptional. They care and keep their cool in the hardest of moments and I hope they recognise how professional and heartwarming it is.

Had several bad experiences with this vets. The booking system for non-urgent appointments is incredibly convoluted and inefficient. They call from a withheld number and don't leave a voicemail and then you're just removed from the list and not contacted any further, without being informed. This even extends to something as simple as trying to reschedule an existing appointment. The email instructions are conflicting and unclear, i.e. told to visit 'the hub' with no explanation as to what the hub is.

The receptionist is incredibly rude, unhelpful and altogether quite patronising and belittling, especially to those who can't afford to make a donation (which seems futile for a service largely applicable for those with low incomes).

Terrible experience on multiple occasions.

I would like to personally thank Will (CSM) who always went out of his way to ensure not only Bear, but also myself were doing Okay throughout such a stressful period. He would always ask how I am doing and is genuinely a caring and personable guy. Adele the Vet who went out of her way to ensure Bears initial operation went ahead and to ensure it was done as quickly as possible. She has such a loving approach and was so understanding around the circumstances myself and Bear was in. I would also like to thank the other vet who completed Bears operations and has followed Bears story right to the end to which Bear is now nearly fully healed. She really cares about the animals she meets and always wants to ensure the correct route of treatment with the best possible outcome is always achieved. Apologies I haven't taken down her name. Also to Kathy, Flo and Danielle RVN's for being absolute angels, Bear is always so trusting of you when you were tending to her wound because of your caring and friendly nature's,  from going that extra mile and giving her hair a trim and her nails and ears to providing additional medical supplies to keep Bear comfortable at home. You really put me at ease when coming along to appointments with Bear. Always trying to make things as easy for me as possible arranging appointments around childcare and school runs. Thank you also to the reception staff and pharmacy who always greeted me with friendliness and respect, whether it be on the phone or face to face. I really can't put into words how grateful I am for everyone's support at Leeds, you are all so very busy, PDSA felt like my second home at times, but your team really do make what is a stressful time, more bearable. I have used the PDSA in Leeds for around five years and unfortunately my recent experience was extremely upsetting. I brought my cat in several times because he had a blocked bladder and a high temperature, which is a serious and potentially life-threatening condition for male cats.

During this time I experienced very poor communication from staff, including being hung up on when I called early in the morning while worried about my cat’s condition. At the appointment I was told my cat needed further tests and treatment, but the situation quickly escalated and I was told I was banned from the premises while my cat was still being treated.

Because of the ban, I had to send someone else in on my behalf while I waited outside, and I was not properly informed about the treatment my cat was given despite asking to be updated beforehand. When he came home he had been given an injection that had not been discussed with me and had a noticeable reaction at the injection site.

Since then I have tried to raise my concerns and speak to higher management, but I have not been given the opportunity to do so. After five years of bringing my pet here, the lack of communication and compassion during such a serious situation was very disappointing.

I can’t thank them enough, I brought my cat Daisy in very poorly. They were able to see her that day, admit her and take good care of her. Unfortunately she was too poorly and passed away but the staff supported us and really helped. I’m autistic and really struggle with mental health condition. The lady vet who took care of my Daisy, also supported me. They were caring, gave us time with Daisy and did everything they could to help.
The lady who answers the phone was initially quite hard to talk to, but after spending time listening to her take calls I understand why, by the sounds of it she’s dealing with a huge amount of difficult calls everyday. I asked my mum to take my cat to the vet, as I was working. She took him and was advised his diabetes had worsened, and some bloods would be needed. He had the bloods taken and the vet told her to come back with him the following day to DISCUSS the results and decide on treatment. Now this is the important part: It was mentioned that perhaps euthanasia may need to be discussed in the future, but she didn’t once say it would actually happen the following day.

My mum went back with him the following day and the vet told her that the bloods didn’t look good, and the options were to have him stay overnight with a drip, or put him to sleep. My mum told the vet he was not her cat, and could not decide without speaking to me so the vet told her to call me. I was in the midst of a 2 hour meeting when this happened so couldn’t answer. My mum explained this to her and said she would bring him home to me and I can call them to let them know once I finish work. The vet then told my mum she could not let her leave with him, as it would be unethical and she would need to put him to sleep. As she couldn’t get hold of me, my mum had no choice but to do what the vet said and he was put to sleep. She then charged my mum £25 for the consultation and a further £25 for putting him to sleep, against our wishes. It would have been £140 to bury/cremate him and my mum didn’t know what to do without asking me so all she could do was take his dead body home to me.

I am in no way saying he shouldn’t have been put to sleep, and had I been there, I likely would have agreed. BUT, my mum was essentially tricked into taking him there by the vet telling her it would be nothing more than a conversation. Thus, robbing me of the chance to say goodbye and euthanising him without my consent. He was eating, drinking, meowing and playing just a few hours before the appointment and a few more hours so I could say goodbye would not have harmed him any further.

For years I donated to PDSA, and I made the mistake of registering him here after our old practice closed down; believing as they were a charity for animals, they would take good care of him. I am absolutely disgusted.
